subject: Post-call: Prompt set collection & model recommendations for Acme
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Prompt set collection & model recommendations for Acme

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Goal: Understand the prompt/edge-case coverage needed for Acme’s internal knowledge assistant pilot and collect real user prompts for evals.
- Key constraints you mentioned: PII redaction required for user-submitted prompts, two primary domains (billing and internal KB search), 99th‑percentile latency target <= 300ms for short prompts, and hard requirement for audit logs retention (7 years).
- Recommended next items from our side: share benchmark comparisons and a prompt collection template; propose candidate model families for initial evals.

Connor will run a short architecture note on latency tradeoffs for the call profile you shared. Rishi and I will stitch together a recommended model + quantization shortlist and a small eval harness.

What we need from you to start the model-fit evals:
1) A CSV or list of representative user prompts (anonymized if needed) covering the top 3 use cases and edge cases (examples: multi‑sentence billing disputes, partial order IDs, ambiguous pronouns).
2) Any internal redaction rules or examples of PII you want removed (or we can apply our redaction guide).
3) Preferred SLA/rollback criteria and success metric (e.g., <= 5% regression in intent detection or >= 90% "helpful" rating in manual eval).

I attached our prompt collection template and a short redaction guidance doc to make this easier. If it's helpful, Connor can run a 30‑minute session to walk your team through how to export and anonymize prompts.

Proposed timing: if you can share the sample prompts by EOD Tue (2026-03-24) we can have an initial fit report back by Thu (2026-03-26). Does that timeline work?

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood_prompt_collection_template.xlsx, redaction_guidelines.pdf

From: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 09:08:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Prompt set collection & model recommendations for Acme

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the summary — timeline looks fine. I attached a CSV (acme_user_prompts.csv) with ~120 prompts pulled from the billing chat transcripts and one small slice of KB search queries. This is masked; we removed full account numbers but left fragments (e.g., last 4 digits) because the assistant needs to handle partial IDs.

A few notes on redaction:
- We need email addresses and full SSNs removed before anything leaves our VPC.
- Customer names can be replaced with the token [CUSTOMER_NAME], but internal agent IDs should stay intact for logging.
- For audit purposes we want to keep a map locally; Redwood’s team asked about how you handle re-IDs — happy to discuss.

Edge cases you’ll see in the CSV:
- Multi-turn billing disputes where the user references previous messages but the text is pasted in a single prompt.
- Messy order IDs that include extra dashes or prefixes.
- Prompts with code blocks (snippets users paste) from our billing tool.

We look forward to the fit report. Quick question: which models do you recommend we try first given the low-latency target and moderate content complexity?

Cheers,
Alicia
Senior PM, Payments — Acme Corp

Attachments: acme_user_prompts.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 11:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Prompt set collection & model recommendations for Acme

Alicia — great, thanks for the CSV and the redaction notes. That gives us exactly what we need to start.

High-level recommended model plan (first pass):
- Candidate 1: Llama-2-13b-chat (8-bit quant) — good balance of quality/throughput for KB + billing semantics.
- Candidate 2: Open-Redwood-7B (4-bit quant, latency-optimized) — for lower latency budgets and higher QPS.
- Candidate 3: a smaller embedding-only flow + retrieval augmentation for long KB context (if you see long documents frequently).

Why this set: the prompts you shared include a mix of short transactional queries and a subset of multi-sentence dispute descriptions. For short prompts with a 300ms P99 target, we suspect the 7B quantized variant + retrieval will meet latency at the cost of a small quality delta; the 13B quantized will be our quality anchor. We'll run both on your prompt set to produce token-level latency, quality scores (semantic similarity + human labeled "helpful"), and regression checks against a small golden set.

Related links we’ll use in the report:
- Benchmark results folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/benchmark_results_ACME
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ACME-2026-01

Next steps from Redwood (targeting the dates we discussed):
1) Connor will run the first latency sweep across your CSV prompts (estimate: 24–36 hours).
2) Rishi and I will run the quality evals and assemble a short report with recommended model + quantization profiles and an initial cost estimate.
3) We’ll include guidance on redaction flows and an optional demo of our re-ID integration.

Question for you: do you want the evaluation to include streaming token-by-token analysis, or is aggregate per-prompt latency sufficient for your SLO calculations? Streaming gives more insight into tail behavior but is heavier to run.

If you’re good with that, we’ll start the sweeps tomorrow morning.

Best,
Marissa

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 10:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Prompt set collection & model recommendations for Acme

Marissa —

Thanks — streaming isn’t necessary for now; aggregate per-prompt latency and a 95/99 percentile breakdown will be enough for our SRE review. Please prioritize the billing subset first (we’ll expand to KB search next week).

Also: on re-ID mapping, we will not share our local map. We just need the redaction guidance and options for on-prem keying for any re-ID if needed.

Confirming: you’ll start the sweeps Thu morning (our time), and we’ll expect the initial fit report by Thu EOD PT.

Appreciate the help — looking forward to the results.

Best,
Alicia

Attachments: none
